verdicts.trueWording: wreck every creative industry, flood the internet with garbage
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched live (robinsloan.com, HTTP 200, browser UA). Passage: 'Can't these companies simply promise ... and meanwhile, wreck every creative industry, flood the internet with garbage, grow rich on the value of Everything? Let us cook - while culture fades into a sort of oatmeal sludge.' Sits exactly where the page hint says, right after 'But what if that isn't the primary application?'. The claim's 'may' is supported by Sloan's follow-on 'They can do that! They probably will.' Chunk supplied no quote string, so nothing to mismatch; the claim's own distinctive wording is on the page word for word.

verdicts.trueWording: Your document doesn't have the same grain, the same umami
verdicts.note: Quote 'The same grain. The same umami.' appears verbatim. Full context: 'I have a hypothesis, which naturally might be wrong: that it is precisely the naivete of Everything, the fact that its writing was actually produced for all those different reasons, that makes it so valuable. Composing a fake corporate email, knowing it will be used to train a language model ... you're not doing the same thing as the real email-writer.' Every limb - hypothesis framing, commissioned/clean-room corpus, writing produced for its own varied reasons - is on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: one important difference from plagiarism: proving it to a legal standard
verdicts.note: neil-clarke.com/ai-and-short-fiction-2/ fetched live (HTTP 200), post dated 07/16/2026. Page: 'The use of generative "AI" in submissions is not the same as plagiarism ... it has one important difference from plagiarism: proving it to a legal standard is significantly more complex. Very few will leave a prompt in or admit what they've done.' Quote verbatim; both limbs (the plagiarism contrast, the prompt/admission rationale) supported; context is indeed the argument against naming names.

verdicts.trueWording: a handful of publishers that are ok with generated slop
verdicts.note: neil-clarke.com/ai-and-short-fiction-1/ fetched live (HTTP 200), post dated 07/14/2026. Final bullet is headed 'YOU MAY DISCOVER THEY DO NOT CARE' and reads: 'There are a handful of publishers that are ok with generated slop. Horrifying, I know. At the bare minimum, they should be transparent about what they are doing and own it, but that's not always the case.' Quote verbatim, both limbs supported, page location exactly as hinted.

verdicts.trueWording: Your first draft isn't an unoriginal idea expressed clearly
verdicts.note: New Yorker page fetched live in full (HTTP 200, datePublished 2023-02-09; article text complete through the closing bullet). Page: 'Your first draft isn't an unoriginal idea expressed clearly; it's an original idea expressed poorly.' Quote verbatim; the claim's two-sided contrast is exactly the sentence's structure, in the passage arguing against starting original work from generated text.

verdicts.trueWording: That's what directs you during rewriting
verdicts.note: Same paragraph as 928: '... accompanied by your amorphous dissatisfaction, your awareness of the distance between what it says and what you want it to say. That's what directs you during rewriting, and that's one of the things lacking when you start with text generated by an A.I.' The supplied quote is a word-for-word prefix of Chiang's sentence (page continues 'it to say'); both limbs - dissatisfaction directs rewriting, and it is lacking when starting from generated text - are explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: rephrases material from the Web instead of quoting it word for word
verdicts.note: Page: 'The fact that ChatGPT rephrases material from the Web instead of quoting it word for word makes it seem like a student expressing ideas in her own words ...; it creates the illusion that ChatGPT understands the material.' Quote verbatim; the causal limb (because it rephrases rather than quotes) is the same sentence. Paragraph is the lossless-vs-lossy explanation, as the page hint says.

verdicts.trueWording: When we're dealing with sequences of words
verdicts.note: Closing sentence of that same paragraph: 'When we're dealing with sequences of words, lossy compression looks smarter than lossless compression.' Quote verbatim and the whole claim is that sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: GPT-3's statistical analysis ... but no more than that
verdicts.note: Page: 'GPT-3's statistical analysis of examples of arithmetic enables it to produce a superficial approximation of the real thing, but no more than that.' Quote verbatim. The 'concludes from GPT-3's arithmetic failures' limb is supported by the preceding sentences - accuracy falling to ten per cent at five digits, and the observation that it doesn't carry the '1'.

verdicts.trueWording: the more that text generated by large language models gets published
verdicts.note: Page: 'the more that text generated by large language models gets published on the Web, the more the Web becomes a blurrier version of itself.' Quote verbatim, in the content-mill passage as hinted. One framing caveat, not a limb failure: Chiang states this as a present-tense dynamic rather than labelling it a prediction (his explicitly labelled 'prediction' two paragraphs later is about GPT-4's training data); written Feb 2023, the sentence is forward-looking, so 'predicted' is fair paraphrase.

verdicts.trueWording: Six tools. The same text. Three entirely different verdicts.
verdicts.note: thenewpublishingstandard.com fetched live (HTTP 200), 'Posted by Mark Williams | Jun 9, 2026'. Section 'The Experiment' lists ZeroGPT 50.9% AI-generated, TextGuard 73% AI-generated, Grammarly 39%, and GPTZero/Quillbot/Copyleaks each 100% human, then 'Six tools. The same text. Three entirely different verdicts.' All figures and the three-100%-human count check out; the tools are described as 'six of the most widely used free AI detection tools'. Minor wording point only: the Cuckoo's Calling run is written in the passive ('were run through'), the first-person 'ran' appears for his other tests.

verdicts.trueWording: was run through Quillbot. The result: 100% AI-generated.
verdicts.note: Page: 'the Gambian national anthem - formal, ceremonial, metrically structured, written by human beings with great deliberate care back in 1965 - was run through Quillbot. The result: 100% AI-generated.' And of the deliberately AI-written answers: 'Quillbot's verdict: 100% human.' Both limbs and the 1965 date verified. The supplied quote, 'formal ceremonial writing is, by design, controlled and consistent', also appears verbatim, in the later explanatory section as the page field indicates.

verdicts.trueWording: AI models ... tend toward uniform sentence lengths
verdicts.note: Page, in the burstiness explanation under 'How The Tools Actually Work': 'AI models, trained on vast corpora of text and optimised for coherence, tend toward uniform sentence lengths - typically fifteen to twenty-five words - with consistent grammatical structures.' Quote verbatim and every limb of the claim is that one sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: produces exactly the statistical signature the tools are trained to flag
verdicts.note: Page: 'Highly polished, professionally edited, obsessively revised human prose looks like AI prose to these tools. Decades of craft, the ruthless elimination of unnecessary words, the achievement of syntactic consistency that every good writing teacher praises - all of this produces exactly the statistical signature the tools are trained to flag.' Quote verbatim; 'these tools' are, in the two preceding paragraphs, defined as measuring perplexity and burstiness, so the claim's 'perplexity-and-burstiness detectors' limb is supported.

verdicts.trueWording: The Gettysburg Address scores as high-probability AI-generated
verdicts.note: The claim's quote is a complete sentence of the article and appears verbatim in the 'How The Tools Actually Work' section, alongside 'Cormac McCarthy has been flagged by these tools.' Note it is Williams's assertion, not a test he reports running (unlike the Cuckoo's Calling and anthem runs); the claim's 'Williams reports that' is neutral enough to stand.
